item.title: COMING THIS Saturday August 29 | Keller & The Keels w/sg Tanasi — Fri Aug 28 — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Saturday, August 29 • 7 PM – 11 PM | From $45.70 Event Details and Tickets Musical Mad Scientist Keller Williams brings his Appalachian Psychedelic Bluegrass project, Keller & the Keels, to the stage on Saturday, August 29 with special guest Tanasi. Joining him are award-winning flatpicker Larry Keel and his rock-solid, in-the-pocket bass-playing wife, Jenny Keel. The trio—formed in 2004—has recorded three albums together (Grass, Thief, and Speed), and with only a handful of shows each year, every performance turns into a joyful, high-energy acoustic picking party. As Keller puts it, “We vowed from the beginning that we wouldn’t do it often so that when we did, it would be special—and it is.” 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of Grass, Keller & the Keels’ first album together. After two decades, Grass finally gets its first-ever vinyl pressing—available on site and ready to roll.

item.title: WNC Sierra Club 9/2: Birds We Love — Wed Sep 2, 7:00 PM
item.description:
WNC Sierra Club Join us Sept. 2 as we host Blue Ridge Audubon member Tom Tribble for a presentation about birds of western North Carolina. Topics will include the value of birds, food requirements, the importance of native plants, the impact of climate change, migration, bird identification tips and interesting facts about some of our local birds. The presentation will conclude with pictures and songs of more than 2 dozen birds found in our region.
The WNC Sierra Club meets monthly in Room 102 at UNCA’s Reuter Center on Campus Drive and simultaneously on [Zoom](https://unca-edu.zoom.us/j/85189349413?pwd=QmorsXPwjbS0BgiLR7xLItF3M1atab.1).
**Parking at UNC Asheville:** If you do not have a parking sticker from OLLI, you'll need to register for parking either ahead of time at [unca.aimsparking.com](https://unca.aimsparking.com/) or at the Reuter Center on the night of the meeting. Creativity lives innately within us all—our natural capacity to imagine, envision new possibilities, and bring fresh energy into our lives. In this two-hour introductory workshop, you’ll be invited into a different kind of art-making: not focused on skill or product, but on expression from within. Held in sacred space and in communion with nature, we’ll explore intuitive painting, journaling, and reflective practices to quiet the mind and awaken your inner creative self—helping you see what may not have been fully acknowledged, and allowing inspiration, clarity, and joy to arise. Many participants are surprised by what unfolds—the unexpected that emerges through the process itself. This introductory session lays the foundation for future workshops. item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: Hawkwatch at Grandfather Mountain — Wed Sep 16, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Hawkwatch at Grandfather Mountain with Lauren Lampley Wednesday, September 16 | 9 am – 3 pm BRN – Elective Register Here!
Ever wonder where our migratory hawks go in the wintertime? Join Arboretum and Grandfather Mountain staff on a day filled with scanning the skies for these migratory birds. There is a chance to see hundreds of migratory hawks as they fly by the mountain on their way south for the winter. During this day we will also talk about the different types of hawks and other birds of prey that migrate following the Appalachian Mountains. This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, you will want to let us know and we will tell you where to meet. This program will take place outside and will follow rocky paths onto the Linville Peak area. item.title: Manifesting Self — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads **Location Change:** **Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**
Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??
Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.
Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.
We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!
Source: AVL Digital Nomads
